chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from his father, raising it, said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who married a slave-girl of a man whose lord had emancipated the first child she gave birth to. So she gave birth to twins. So he said: 'Both of them are emancipated'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the emancipation of twins if the firstborn is freed?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that both twins are emancipated because the condition of the firstborn's birth triggered the mother's manumission, which extends to the second twin born simultaneously. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'Umm al-Walad' (mother of the child) and demonstrates the practical application of conditional emancipation in early Islamic society. It underscores the emphasis on liberating slaves through progeny, a key theme in Shia legal theory.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Hashimy, from his father, raising it,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who married a child of a man whose lord had emancipated the first child she gave birth to. So she gave birth to twins. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Both of them are emancipated’.
